scenario: AITA For Selling My Former Roommates Games | So a few years ago I was renting this place with this dude and we were on a lease. When the lease was nearing it's end he just peaced out. We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me break it down step by step.

First, the situation: The user was rooming with someone, and when the lease was ending, the roommate left without taking most of his belongings. The user tried to contact him for two weeks to pick up his stuff, but he didn't respond. The user then took most of the roommate's things to the dump, but kept the video games. He sold them to a local store for $600. Now, the roommate is upset and calling him an asshole, asking for the money back. Legally, there's nothing the roommate can do, but the user is wondering if he's the asshole morally.

So, the main question is: Is it morally acceptable for the user to sell his former roommate's video games after the roommate didn't respond to repeated attempts to contact him?

Let me think about the possible moral principles involved here. One is the concept of ownership. The games belong to the roommate, right? So, selling them without permission might be seen as theft or at least a violation of the roommate's property rights. On the other hand, the roommate abandoned his stuff, and the user was trying to get him to pick it up, but he didn't. So, maybe the user felt justified in getting rid of the stuff, including selling the games.

Another angle is the concept of responsibility. The roommate was supposed to take his belongings when moving out. By not doing so, he left the user in a difficult position. The user had to deal with the stuff, and the landlord was going to charge him if he didn't dispose of it. So, the user took the initiative to get rid of the stuff, which might be seen as responsible.

But then, selling the games for $600 seems like a significant amount. The roommate is upset because he lost his games, and he's asking for the money back. The user is legally in the clear, but morally, is it right to keep the money?

I think it's important to consider the intentions and the outcomes. The user's intention was to handle the situation responsibly, trying to contact the roommate and then taking action to avoid being charged by the landlord. Selling the games was a way to dispose of them and maybe even make some money. But the roommate's reaction shows that he felt wronged because his property was sold without his consent.

So, from a moral standpoint, even though the user had good intentions and was legally justified, taking someone else's property and selling it without their permission might still be considered wrong. It's a violation of trust and property rights, even if the roommate was negligent in the first place.

Therefore, I would lean towards the action being morally unacceptable because it involved selling someone else's belongings without their consent, even if the user had tried to contact the roommate beforehand.
